description: The Risk-Screening Environmental Indicators (RSEI) model is an EPA screening tool that combines Toxics Release Inventory data with other sources to put toxic chemical releases and waste management into a relative, risk-based context, calculating scores that point to chronic human health risks. Results help policy makers, researchers and communities set priorities for further investigation, identify chemicals and industrial facilities of greatest concern and follow changes in potential health impacts over time. It is produced by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, which offers the EasyRSEI web dashboard, version 2.3.12 at access, RSEI microdata, a methodology document, microdata documentation and a data dictionary; the page was last updated on 25 August 2026. Coverage is US facilities that report to the Toxics Release Inventory. Results are available free online through the dashboard and as microdata downloads. Caveats: scores are relative screening values, not risk estimates, and depend on what facilities report to the Toxics Release Inventory. For simulation it ranks industrial sites by potential chronic health impact for exposure analyses around chemical plants and for scenarios of where emission changes matter most. It is related to the EPA Toxics Release Inventory record in this catalogue, its main input.
